title: Make sure that each messaging channel has its own session
body:
<!--
## For Automatticians!

:wave: Just a quick reminder that this is a public repo. Please don't include any internal links or sensitive data (like PII, private code, customer names, site URLs, etc. Any fixes related to security should be discussed with Platform before opening a PR. If you're not sure if something is safe to share, please just ask!

## For external contributors!

Welcome! We look forward to your contribution! ❤️
-->
## Description
<!--
A few sentences providing more context and describing the overall goals of the Pull Request.

Should include any special considerations, decisions, and links to relevant publicly available sources (e.g. GitHub issues)
-->

This PR ensures that 2 or more WordPress site that belongs to the same Salesforce org doesn't share the same chat session. Without this PR, 2 or more WordPress site that belongs to the same Salesforce org **will share the same chat session**

We need to have a different session so that the prechat field are different, because prechat fields are session-based and not real-time. Also, it's a UX kind of a problem - it's weird to see the same bot and conversation that was on Site A appear on Site B.

One caveat with this integration is that we can no longer continue the session after the tab has closed if the user has two sites under the same Salesforce org open.

## Pre-review checklist

Please make sure the items below have been covered before requesting a review:

- [ ] This change works and has been tested locally or in Codespaces (or has an appropriate fallback).
- [ ] This change has relevant unit tests (if applicable).
- [ ] This change has relevant documentation additions / updates (if applicable).
- [ ] I've created a changelog description that aligns with the provided examples.

## Pre-deploy checklist

- [ ] VIP staff: Ensure any alerts added/updated conform to internal standards (see internal documentation).

## Steps to Test

For testing, we can use the scratch org that i've setup.

1. Before anything, checkout the branch and run `npm run build:dev`
1. Add these to `env.php`:

```php
<?php
$embedding_script_123 = <<<'ESW'
<script type='text/javascript'>
	function initEmbeddedMessaging() {
		try {
			embeddedservice_bootstrap.settings.language = 'en_US'; // For example, enter 'en' or 'en-US'

			embeddedservice_bootstrap.init(
				'00Dcb00000BhF2K',
				'WP_123_1_vip_agentforce_123_vipdev_lndo',
				'https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.site.com/ESWWP1231vipagentforc1772558583071',
				{
					scrt2URL: 'https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.salesforce-scrt.com'
				}
			);
		} catch (err) {
			console.error('Error loading Embedded Messaging: ', err);
		}
	};
</script>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.site.com/ESWWP1231vipagentforc1772558583071/assets/js/bootstrap.min.js' onload='initEmbeddedMessaging()'></script>

ESW;

$embedding_script_124 = <<<'ESW'
<script type='text/javascript'>
	function initEmbeddedMessaging() {
		try {
			embeddedservice_bootstrap.settings.language = 'en_US'; // For example, enter 'en' or 'en-US'

			embeddedservice_bootstrap.init(
				'00Dcb00000BhF2K',
				'WP_124_1_vip_agentforce_124_vipdev_lndo',
				'https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.site.com/ESWWP1241vipagentforc1772560601610',
				{
					scrt2URL: 'https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.salesforce-scrt.com'
				}
			);
		} catch (err) {
			console.error('Error loading Embedded Messaging: ', err);
		}
	};
</script>
<script type='text/javascript' src='https://ruby-speed-1539-dev-ed.scratch.my.site.com/ESWWP1241vipagentforc1772560601610/assets/js/bootstrap.min.js' onload='initEmbeddedMessaging()'></script>

ESW;


// Fake config for the mock API (use any URL, it will be intercepted)
define( 'VIP_AGENTFORCE_CONFIGS', json_encode( [
    'ingestion_api_instance_url' => 'https://hfrtknb-myzt8mrwg03tkzdgh0.c360a.salesforce.com',
    'ingestion_api_token'        => "snip",
    'ingestion_api_source_name'  => 'vip_agentforce_wp_post',
    'ingestion_api_object_name'  => 'wordpress_post',
    // Add preset hook config here (see Test Cases below)
    // 'ingestion_api_sync_all_posts' => true,
    'ingestion_api_categories'   => [ 'animals' ],
    'agentforce_js_sdk_activated' => true,
    'agentforce_embedding_script' => str_contains( $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] ?? '', 'vip-agentforce-124' ) ? $embedding_script_124 : $embedding_script_123,
] ) );
```
2. Create two environments - `vip-agentforce-123` and `vip-agentforce-124` i.e:
```
vip dev-env create --slug=vip-agentforce-123
vip dev-env start --slug=vip-agentforce-123
vip dev-env create --slug=vip-agentforce-124
vip dev-env start --slug=vip-agentforce-124
```
3. Open https://vip-agentforce-123.vipdev.lndo.site - make sure it's the `https` site.
4. Open the developer console (F12 usually) and run `window.AgentforceCMP.loadSDK()`.
5. Wait for the widget to load, click the widget bubble, wait for the agent to say something, and then say 'Hello!'
6. Now, on a new tab, open https://vip-agentforce-124.vipdev.lndo.site - make sure it's the `https` site.
7. Open the developer console (F12 usually) and run `window.AgentforceCMP.loadSDK()`.
8. Wait for the widget to load, click the widget bubble, **ensure that you get a new session, and you don't see the session from the vip-agentforce-123 domain**.

Without this PR,  step number 8 would instead show you the same session for both `vip-agentforce-123` and `vip-agentforce-124`.

title: Fix flaky Q4 of 03753_join_runtime_filter_dynamically_disable
body:
<!--
Linked issues and pull requests. Use full GitHub URLs, one relationship per line; delete the lines you don't need.

Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/111972
Related: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/106734
-->


### Changelog category (leave one):
- CI Fix or Improvement (changelog entry is not required)


### Changelog entry (a [user-readable short description](https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/docs/changelog_entry_guidelines.md) of the changes that goes into CHANGELOG.md):
...


### Description

`03753_join_runtime_filter_dynamically_disable` fails on the **Q4** line only, printing `Q4 0 ...`
instead of `Q4 1 Ok`
([sighting](https://s3.amazonaws.com/clickhouse-test-reports/json.html?PR=111405&sha=52132ba17e43cd9d589e2988df497eefc4ccc10d&name_0=PR&name_1=Stateless%20tests%20%28amd_debug%2C%20parallel%29)).

**Root cause.** Q4 asserts `RuntimeFilterBlocksProcessed = 0`, which only the bloom filter reaches,
via `setFullyDisabled()` on over-fill. With `join_runtime_filter_from_fixed_hash_table` on,
`HashJoin::publishSharedRuntimeFilters` replaces that fully disabled bloom filter with a
`SharedFixedHashTableRuntimeFilter`, which has no full-disable path. Q4's probe keys all lie inside
the build range, so every row passes and only the pass-ratio heuristic throttles: the failing run
recorded `Processed = 12 / Skipped = 290`. `Processed = 0` is unreachable there.

**Onset is #111972**, as @ m-selmi identified in review.
`max_bytes_ratio_before_external_join` defaults to 0.5, so `SpillingHashJoin` wraps the join by
default and used to inherit `hasPostBuildPhase() = false`, which kept the shared filter unpublished.
A/B on one host, one test file, one server configuration: with those two overrides removed the
unpinned test passes 8 of 8 runs in one process; with them it passes the first run then fails 7 of 7
at `Processed = 12`, byte-identical to CI. CIDB shows 5 such failures across 5 PRs within 8 hours of
that merge, none in the preceding 45 days. The first run passes because the arm is
chosen from the process-global hash-table statistics cache, which is also why this is invisible on
master and shows up only in `parallel` jobs.

**The change** pins `join_runtime_filter_from_fixed_hash_table = 0` for the file, selecting the
implementation whose disabling behaviour Q4 exists to test. It costs no coverage: only Q4 ever
reaches the shared-filter arm (3 runs, 3 publications, all `log_comment = Q4`), and the other six
queries give identical counters pinned and unpinned. `04241` remains that arm's dedicated test.

**Validation.** 40 of 40 runs pass (20 randomized, 20 not); removing the pin reddens it 5 of 5.

Noticed, not filed: `SharedFixedHashTableRuntimeFilter` has no full-disable path at all.


<!-- ch-version-info:start -->
### Version info
- Merged into: `26.8.1.1181` (included in `26.8` and later)
<!-- ch-version-info:end -->

title: feat(enrollment): standalone single-use site-token enrollment service
body:
[Design doc:](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1B8ym7zaGtbmHER7jF1Z2xWKo8h8HKYvvO0lCM-hjF0o/edit?tab=t.0)

## Summary

Enrollment is one synchronous exchange. A grid-admin mints a single-use token that pins a site name, and a site redeems it with a certificate signing request to receive a signed certificate, the grid CA certificate, and an enrollment id in the same response. The flow has no approval queue and no request lifecycle. The grid, not the requester, assigns the member name.

## Motivation

Before this, a requester could POST a CSR and ask for another site's name in the body, receiving a certificate for it if an operator approved. Pinning the name at mint and gating enrollment behind the token closes that: no unauthenticated party can enroll, and the name comes only from the grid-admin's pin. Collapsing the approval lifecycle into a single redeem also removes the queue, the phases, and the joining kit, so the grant is identity only.

## What changed

- Three flat endpoints. `POST /v1alpha1/enrollmenttokens` (grid-admin) mints a one-time 256-bit token from the system CSPRNG, stores only its digest, and returns the token once. `DELETE /v1alpha1/enrollmenttokens/{id}` revokes one that leaked. `POST /v1alpha1/enrollments` (site) redeems a token and a CSR. Both credentials ride in `Authorization: Bearer`, and the RBAC resource name equals the URL segment.
- The enroll body carries only the CSR. The token is validated before any CSR crypto, the CSR is verified for possession of the key, and the token is redeemed and the certificate signed and recorded in one transaction stamped with the pinned name. A failed sign or insert rolls the redeem back, so the token is spent if and only if the certificate is issued.
- The response returns the signed certificate, the grid CA certificate, and an enrollment id. The certs primitive rebuilds every SAN from the pinned name, so a CSR cannot assert a name of its own. The grid CA is not served from its own endpoint.
- The service terminates TLS in-process (axum-server with rustls) and refuses to start without TLS material, so a CA-signing endpoint never serves in the clear. The server certificate reloads from disk on an interval, so a rotated secret is served without a restart.
- The Postgres connection must require TLS. A connection string whose sslmode permits a plaintext fallback (disable, allow, prefer) is refused at startup.
- On SIGINT or SIGTERM the service drains in-flight requests before it exits, and a per-request timeout bounds handler and body-read time.
- Token authorization is a write verb on a distinct RBAC resource, so a read-only grid-admin cannot mint or revoke. The resource is derived from the matched route and fails closed for any route added later.
- A Postgres advisory lock serializes schema application, so two instances starting at once do not race on the table's implicit type.

Coverage: the HTTP flow end to end plus its security properties, the mint-to-issued lifecycle, and concurrent redeem and same-name races against a real Postgres.

The `api/enrollment-v1alpha1.yaml` spec still describes the earlier lifecycle design and is rewritten in a follow-up. The deploy README describes the shipped endpoints meanwhile.

This is the single enrollment PR. The earlier split (#151 service core, #152 wire-type codegen) is folded into it and those PRs are closed.

Part of #150.

title: feat(python): emit PEP 639 license metadata in generated pyproject.toml
body:
## Description
`metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }` already works for the Java SDK generator (name extracted from the file into the POM `licenses` block). The Python generator accepted the same config and copied the LICENSE file into the repo, but wrote nothing about it into `pyproject.toml`.

License metadata is now emitted in the `[project]` table following [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) (the form the requesting customer asked for):

```toml
# metadata.license: "Apache-2.0"
[project]
license = "Apache-2.0"

# metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }  (unrecognized text)
[project]
license-files = ["LICENSE"]

# metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }  (file contains Apache-2.0 / MIT / BSD / GPL / MPL / ISC text)
[project]
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
```

The `license = "MIT"` / `"Apache-2.0"` line moves from `[tool.poetry]` to `[project]` (poetry-core ≥2.0 reads it as a license expression; the generated `[project]` table already requires poetry-core 2.x). The `License :: OSI Approved :: ...` classifiers for MIT/Apache are unchanged.

For custom files, the generator reads the license text (from `<output>/<filename>` or the `/tmp/LICENSE` mount used by local generation) and applies the same substring heuristics as the Java generator (`GeneratedBuildGradle`). A recognized license additionally gets `license = "<SPDX>"` and the matching PyPI classifier; unrecognized text stays file-only with no guessed classifier (the file could be proprietary, etc.). This gives Java parity from a single config key: `custom: ./LICENSE` with Apache text → id + file in both generators.

Resulting sdist metadata (poetry-core 2.5): `License-Expression: Apache-2.0` for basic licenses; `License-File: LICENSE` (and the file packaged) for custom, plus `License-Expression` when recognized.

## Changes Made
- `license_detector.py` (new): `detect_spdx_license(content)` / `detect_spdx_license_from_file(*paths)` mirroring Java's patterns (Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-3/2-Clause, GPL-3.0/2.0-only, MPL-2.0, ISC) + `SPDX_CLASSIFIERS` map
- `pyproject_toml.py`: `_get_project_license()` emits `license = "<SPDX>"` for `BasicLicense`; for `CustomLicense` emits `license-files = ["<filename>"]` (TOML-escaped) preceded by `license = "<detected SPDX>"` when recognized; the `[tool.poetry]` `license` line is removed
- `pypi_classifier_creator.py`: `create_classifiers(..., detected_spdx_license=)` adds the classifier for a recognized custom license
- Seed: new `exhaustive/custom-license` output folder for `python-sdk` (mirrors the existing Java fixture) + generated snapshot (fixture LICENSE is unrecognized → file-only)
- Changelog entry in `generators/python/sdk/changes/unreleased/`
- [ ] Updated README.md generator (not applicable)

body_clean:
## Description
`metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }` already works for the Java SDK generator (name extracted from the file into the POM `licenses` block). The Python generator accepted the same config and copied the LICENSE file into the repo, but wrote nothing about it into `pyproject.toml`.

License metadata is now emitted in the `[project]` table following [PEP 639](https://peps.python.org/pep-0639/) (the form the requesting customer asked for):

```toml
# metadata.license: "Apache-2.0"
[project]
license = "Apache-2.0"

# metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }  (unrecognized text)
[project]
license-files = ["LICENSE"]

# metadata.license: { custom: "./LICENSE" }  (file contains Apache-2.0 / MIT / BSD / GPL / MPL / ISC text)
[project]
license = "Apache-2.0"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
```

The `license = "MIT"` / `"Apache-2.0"` line moves from `[tool.poetry]` to `[project]` (poetry-core ≥2.0 reads it as a license expression; the generated `[project]` table already requires poetry-core 2.x). The `License :: OSI Approved :: ...` classifiers for MIT/Apache are unchanged.
